name: Saint Bede the Venerable
history: A monk of Jarrow in Northumbria who scarcely left his monastery, yet became one of the most learned men in Europe. His Ecclesiastical History of the English People is the chief source for the conversion of England, and he made dating from the birth of Christ widely known. He is the only English Doctor of the Church.
life: Bede was born on lands belonging to the monastery of Wearmouth and was given to its abbot, Benedict Biscop, at the age of seven. He moved to the new house at Jarrow under Ceolfrith, and spent the rest of his life there, ordained deacon at nineteen and priest at thirty. He wrote of himself that his delight had always been to learn, to teach and to write. He commented on most of the Bible, wrote on time, grammar and the reckoning of Easter, composed lives of saints and poetry, and in 731 finished his history of the English Church. His disciple Cuthbert described his death: he was translating Saint John’s Gospel into English, finished the last sentence, and died on the floor of his cell singing the Glory Be, on the eve of the Ascension, 735. His relics lie in Durham Cathedral. Leo XIII named him a Doctor in 1899.
prayerTo: Saint Bede, you gave your whole life to learning, teaching and praising God in the cloister. Pray for England, for scholars and teachers, and for monks and nuns. Help me to love the Scriptures, to do my work faithfully to the end, and to die, as you did, giving glory to God. Amen.
penance: Read a chapter of Saint John’s Gospel today, the book Bede was translating as he died, and end your work with the Glory Be.
meditation: In Bede’s History a counsellor of King Edwin compares our life to a sparrow flying through a lit hall in winter, in at one door and out at the other. What do you know of where you are going?
